headline: Sox Welcome Powerhouse Braves To Fenway Looking To Turn Things Around
morning_brew: The Red Sox are sitting at twenty-two and thirty, holding down last place in the American League East. Tonight, the Atlanta Braves come to Fenway Park to start a three-game series. Atlanta is thirty-six and eighteen, leading the National League East, so this is going to be a massive test for our guys. We need to find some sort of spark before this stretch completely gets away from us, because hovering eight games under five hundred before June is a tough spot to climb out of.

Over in Foxborough, the focus remains entirely on Drake Maye as he prepares for his second year under offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels. The Patriots finished last season at eight and nine, missing the postseason, and everyone knows the franchise hinges on the development of the young quarterback. McDaniels has to build a system that protects Maye and lets him make plays. It is a vital sophomore campaign for the kid, and the work starts now if they want to compete in a loaded division.

Meanwhile, both the Celtics and Bruins are deep in the off-season after disappointing first-round exits earlier this month. The Bruins got bounced by the Sabres, and the Celtics fell to the 76ers, leaving both franchises with plenty of questions to answer this summer. With the NBA draft and free agency looming, the front office at the Garden needs to be aggressive. We cannot afford to sit back and watch other teams build contenders while we stand pat.
